qr.label: [02] Quick read
qr.title: What I do
qr.p1: I recently worked on a multitenant platform with RAG, embeddings and a vector database for AI, integrating multiple CRM, ERP, marketing and social media platforms. We started with function calling directly on the endpoints and later migrated to an MCP Server, isolating each integration as its own tool. The biggest challenge was handling rate limits and completely different data formats across these integrations — solved by normalizing everything into a single schema while keeping the code simple, without unnecessary complexity.

about.head_title: A full-stack engineer with an infra bias, a product instinct, and attention to trade-offs.

bio.p1: I design and deliver SaaS systems built for reliability and scalability. Laravel is my foundation, but my work spans the entire stack — from data modeling and database optimization to state management and production infrastructure.
bio.p2: Since 2023 at Clickweb, I evolved from intern to full-stack pleno with focus on systems that scale. Deep in infrastructure: CI/CD pipelines, containerization (Docker, Kubernetes), nginx, Linux hardening, observability and disaster recovery. Responsible for keeping mission-critical applications in production — when uptime is non-negotiable, I design and manage the infrastructure.
bio.p3: Architecture is about trade-offs, not dogma. Every technical decision has a cost: performance vs. maintainability, abstraction vs. simplicity, flexibility vs. velocity. The best decisions come when I understand why the business chooses a path — what are the real constraints, what's the timeline, what's the risk of failure. Code elegance without business impact is a luxury that growing teams cannot afford.
bio.p4: Continuous learning is non-negotiable. I read academic papers, technical documentation, protocol RFCs, commit histories from high-performance projects. Currently: transformers and LLMs — tokenization, attention mechanisms, modern architectures. Not about following trends; it's about building genuine expertise. Understanding deeply — not superficially — how things really work.
bio.quote: "If you can't explain the decision to the person paying the bill, you probably haven't finished thinking about it."

p01.d: The cleverest solution is the one the team can debug at 3am without me.

p02.d: A schema that can't encode a broken state costs less than the test suite for catching one.

p03.d: No performance work starts before the metric exists to measure it.

p04.t: Ship the seam before the feature.
p04.d: The interfaces compound. The features get rewritten. Design the interfaces first.

p05.t: Own the whole stack, respect each layer.
p05.d: Generalism isn't an excuse to be shallow — it's permission to go deep where the problem is.
